turns.question: Where are streaming responses implemented, and which public API methods route into the streaming implementation?
turns.text:
I'll investigate the openai-node repository structure to find streaming implementation.Now let's find the public API methods that route into streaming — chat completions, responses, and assistants/beta.I now have a complete picture. Here's the answer.

## Core streaming implementation

**`src/core/streaming.ts`** — the `Stream<Item>` class (SSE parsing over `fetch`/`ReadableStream`).
- `Stream.fromSSEResponse()` (line 34): parses Server-Sent Events from a `Response`, yielding parsed JSON items, handling `[DONE]` sentinels and error events.
- `Stream.fromReadableStream()` (line 108): parses newline-delimited JSON from a raw `ReadableStream` (used by Azure/other transports).
- `_iterSSEMessages` (module-level helper) does the actual byte-decoding/line-splitting via `LineDecoder` (`src/internal/decoders/line.ts`).

**`src/internal/parse.ts`** — `defaultParseResponse()` (line 18) is the dispatch point: every API response funnels through here, and when `props.options.stream` is truthy it calls `props.options.__streamClass.fromSSEResponse(...)` (or `Stream.fromSSEResponse` by default). This is wired into request handling via `APIPromise` (`src/core/api-promise.ts`), which uses `defaultParseResponse` as its default parser, fed by `OpenAI.makeRequest()` in `src/client.ts` (line 752).

So the pipeline is: **resource method → `client.post(path, { stream: true, ... })` → `makeRequest` → `defaultParseResponse` → `Stream.fromSSEResponse`**.

## Higher-level streaming helpers (in `src/lib/`)

Built on top of the raw `Stream<Item>`:
- `ChatCompletionStream.ts` — accumulates chat completion chunks into a final message (`ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion`, line 161).
- `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.ts` / `AbstractChatCompletionRunner.ts` — tool-calling runner loop with streaming.
- `AssistantStream.ts` — Assistants API run streaming (`createAssistantStream`, `createToolAssistantStream`, `createThreadAssistantStream`).
- `responses/ResponseStream.ts` — `ResponseStream.createResponse()` (line 78), accumulates Responses-API events into a final parsed `Response`.
- `EventStream.ts` — shared base class (`_run`, event-emitter semantics, `connect`/`end`/`abort` lifecycle) used by both `ChatCompletionStream` and `ResponseStream`.

Note: `src/realtime/` is a separate WebSocket-based streaming path (Realtime API) and does not use `Stream.fromSSEResponse`; I did not dig into its internals.

## Public API methods that route into streaming

| Method | File | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `client.chat.completions.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/chat/completions/completions.ts:73-79` | returns `APIPromise<Stream<ChatCompletionChunk>>` |
| `client.chat.completions.stream(body)` | same file, line 221-225 | `ChatCompletionStream.createChatCompletion` |
| `client.chat.completions.runTools({stream:true})` | line 196-217 | `ChatCompletionStreamingRunner.runTools` |
| `client.responses.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/responses/responses.ts:105-123` | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.retrieve({stream:true})` | same file, line 137-168 | `Stream<ResponseStreamEvent>` |
| `client.responses.stream(body)` | line 201-205 | `ResponseStream.createResponse` |
| `client.images.edit({stream:true})` | `src/resources/images.ts:54-61` | `Stream<ImageEditStreamEvent>` |
| `client.images.generate({stream:true})` | same file, line 87-93 | `Stream<ImageGenStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.create({stream:true})` | `src/resources/beta/threads/runs/runs.ts:72-82` | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.stream(...)` / `.createAndStream(...)` (deprecated) | same file, line 165-233 | `AssistantStream.createAssistantStream` |
| `client.beta.threads.runs.submitToolOutputs({stream:true})` / `.submitToolOutputsStream(...)` | same file, line 246-299 | `Stream<AssistantStreamEvent>` / `AssistantStream.createToolAssistantStream` |
| legacy `client.completions.create({stream:true})` | referenced in `client.ts` (`CompletionCreateParamsStreaming`) | `Stream<Completion>` — not independently opened, inferred from consistent pattern |

Every one of these ultimately sets `stream: <bool>` on the request options object passed to `this._client.post(...)`, which `defaultParseResponse` inspects to decide whether to hand back a parsed JSON object or a `Stream` instance.

## What I did not verify
- Did not open `src/resources/completions.ts` (legacy Completions API) directly — inferred its streaming wiring from the identical pattern used elsewhere and the type references in `client.ts`.
- Did not inspect `src/realtime/*` internals (WebSocket streaming) beyond confirming the directory exists — it's architecturally distinct (no SSE/`Stream` class involved).
- Did not verify `src/azure.ts` or `src/bedrock.ts` provider-specific streaming behavior.
- Did not run the code; all conclusions are from static reading of source via `gh api`.
